releases.name: Sailing now
releases.blurb: What is in the build you are playing.

items.title: San Francisco Bay, replayed
items.text: Real wind, gusts, tide and tidal stream from NOAA for 14 July 2024, with real depths, coastline and the bridges.

items.title: Three boats
items.text: A 30 ft sloop, a 38 and a 45 ft performance cruiser, each with her own polar, heel and handling. Name her and choose her colours.

items.title: Hands on the boat
items.text: Steer, trim and tack by pointing at the wheel, boom and winches. No sailing buttons on the screen.

items.title: Autopilot and crew
items.text: Hold a heading, a wind angle or the route while the crew trims. It beats to windward and tacks for the mark.

items.title: Chartplotter and passage plan
items.text: Waypoints, leg times from the forecast, plan against actual, and a forecast you can scrub through.

items.title: Sailing in company, first cut
items.text: Open the same link as a friend and see each other's boats live, on one clock, and hail each other.

items.title: First lesson and coaching hints
items.text: An optional guided first sail, then quiet hints when a sail has been luffing for a while or the boat is stuck in irons.

items.title: Point of sail on the instruments
items.text: The readout names what she is doing: close-hauled, beam reach, running, in irons, and which tack.

items.title: Places to sail to
items.text: McCovey Cove, Ayala Cove, Sam's in Tiburon and more are on the chart. Click one to head there.

items.title: Skipper's logbook
items.text: Miles, hours, marks and knockdowns, added up across every sail and shown beside the rest of the fleet.

items.title: Crash gybes
items.text: Let the boom come across on its own in a breeze and she rounds up, or goes flat on her side.

items.title: Gust warnings
items.text: The readout shows a gust on its way and how long until it arrives. A strong one raises an alert and drops time back to real speed.

items.title: Release notes
items.text: What's new lists every update, and a marker tells you when there is one you have not read.

items.title: Racing, first cut
items.text: Call a race or join one: a course, a countdown, pace boats on the autopilot, live places and a finish time.

items.title: Wind tunnel view
items.text: The air over your sails drawn as smoke lines, and the wind angle your trim is asking for. Scott's idea.

items.title: Who is on the water
items.text: A list of every boat sailing with you, what she is doing, and her range and bearing.

releases.name: Release 1 · The Bay together
releases.blurb: The first target. Many people on the same Bay at once, racing or just out for a sail.

items.title: Accounts and profiles
items.text: Sign up with an email. Your skipper profile, boats, fit-out and logbook live with your account, on any device. The logbook in this build is the first piece.

items.title: Race days
items.text: Start lines with a penalty for being over early, mark rounding rules, fleets by boat class, a season table, and results that every boat agrees on.

items.title: A shared Bay to roam
items.text: Drop in any time and see who else is out and where they are on the chart. No race needed: just go sailing together.

items.title: Meet up somewhere
items.text: Pick a place and tell the others: McCovey Cove for the ball game, Ayala Cove on Angel Island, the dock at Sam's in Tiburon.

items.title: Dock, anchor and go ashore
items.text: Come alongside or drop the hook, take the dinghy or kayak in, and walk into the bar. Docking and anchoring done by hand.

items.title: Talk to the fleet
items.text: Text hails are in. Next: voice on a VHF channel, so it sounds like the real thing.

items.title: Its own home on the web
items.text: Regatta on its own website, with a server behind it for shared water, races and accounts. The build is going onto Vercel now.

items.title: Crab pots and fishing
items.text: Anchor, drop a pot and come back to check it. Dungeness in the Bay, tuna offshore. A good catch lifts the crew's morale and stretches the provisions.

releases.name: Release 2 · Passages
releases.blurb: Long races and deliveries that run for days, like a flight simulator for the sea.

items.title: The Baja Ha-Ha
items.text: San Diego to Cabo San Lucas with two stops: a rally start, then days at sea in real time.

items.title: Watches and crew
items.text: Set a watch schedule. Crew have skill and fatigue, and a tired watch misses a wind shift.

items.title: Provisions and tanks
items.text: Load water, food and fuel before you go. Run short and it costs you.

items.title: Call me when she needs me
items.text: Leave her on autopilot and get a text or an email when the wind shifts, a reef is due or land is near.

items.title: Night in port
items.text: Pick up a mooring or take a berth at each stop, sleep, and start the next leg in the morning.

items.title: Out the Gate to the Farallones
items.text: Fifty-two miles of ocean swell, the bar and fog, as the first step offshore.

items.title: Feeding the crew
items.text: What you catch and what you stowed decide what is for dinner, and a fed crew stands a better watch.

releases.name: Release 3 · Charter waters
releases.blurb: Warm water, short hops and a catamaran.

items.title: The 42 ft catamaran
items.text: No heel to warn you: reef by the numbers. Two engines for docking.

items.title: British Virgin Islands
items.text: Line-of-sight island hopping, anchoring and mooring balls.

items.title: Greece
items.text: The Cyclades and the meltemi, stern-to in a harbour for dinner.

items.title: Croatia
items.text: The Dalmatian islands, with the bora and the maestral.

items.title: Logbook and experience
items.text: Miles, night hours and heavy-weather hours earn experience, the way a real logbook does.

items.title: Prize money
items.text: Win races, earn a purse.

items.title: Upgrade the boat
items.text: New sails, a spinnaker, a folding prop, better instruments: each one changes how she sails.

releases.name: Always · Seamanship and the real world
releases.blurb: Making the sailing truer, release after release.

items.title: Sail any day in the archive
items.text: Pick a date, right up to yesterday, and get that day's real wind and tide from NOAA's records. Never live feeds.

items.title: Reefing and furling by hand
items.text: The physics is done. It needs a mast and a furler you can work.

items.title: A better coach
items.text: Hints that notice more: pinching, sailing by the lee, a missed layline, a foul tide you could have dodged.

items.title: Laylines and tide gates on the chart
items.text: See when to tack and when the stream turns in your favour.

items.title: Night and fog
items.text: Navigation lights, lit buoys, the city at night, and San Francisco's fog.

items.title: Spinnakers
items.text: An asymmetric first, then a pole, guys and a preventer.

items.title: What you would really see
items.text: Sea lions on the buoys, pelicans, harbour porpoise in the Gate, humpbacks and greys off the coast in season. Each water gets its own.

releases.name: Other voyages · Different games on the same sea
releases.blurb: Not Regatta, but built on the same water, wind and seamanship. Vote if you would play them.

items.title: The age of sail
items.text: Magellan's circumnavigation or a voyage of your own in a square-rigger: provision for months, keep a crew alive, and find your way by compass, lead line, sextant and stars.

items.title: Shackleton's boat journey
items.text: Eight hundred miles of Southern Ocean in a 22 ft lifeboat, with four sun sights and no margin.

items.title: Pirates of the Caribbean trade
items.text: Spanish, Dutch and British ships, islands to hide and refit in, and prizes to take. Sailing a ship in a fight, with the wind gauge deciding it.
